question: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced Atmanirbhar Clean Plant Programme with an outlay of __________ to boost availability of disease-free and quality planting material for high value horticultural crops.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs 2,200 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced the Atmanirbhar Clean Plant Programme.
 
• The programme has an outlay of Rs 2,200 crore.
 
• It aims to boost the availability of disease-free and quality planting material for high value horticultural crops.
 
• This initiative is part of the larger Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India) campaign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India)**

 
 
• It is a vision of the Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi of making India a self-reliant nation.
 
• It aims to make the country and its citizens independent and self-reliant in all senses.
 
• The initiative focuses on five pillars: economy, infrastructure, system, vibrant demography, and demand.
 
• Various schemes and policies have been introduced under this initiative to promote local manufacturing, reduce dependency on imports, and boost economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Horticulture**
 
 
• Horticulture is the branch of agriculture that deals with the art, science, technology, and business of plant cultivation.
 
• This includes the cultivation of fruits, vegetables, nuts, seeds, herbs, sprouts, mushrooms, algae, flowers, seaweeds, and non-food crops such as grass and ornamental trees and plants.
 
• Horticultural crops are diverse; they include annual and perennial species, fruits and vegetables, and decorative indoor plants.
 
• Horticulture plays a vital role in the economy by providing employment opportunities and contributing significantly to the GDP.
 
 
 
• **Disease-Free Planting Material**
 
 
• Disease-free planting material refers to plants or plant parts that are free from pathogens and pests that can cause diseases.
 
• The use of such material is crucial in horticulture to ensure healthy crop production and high yields.
 
• It helps in reducing the spread of diseases, ensuring the production of quality crops, and increasing the overall productivity of the horticultural sector.
 
• Programs like the Atmanirbhar Clean Plant Programme aim to promote the use of disease-free planting material to enhance agricultural productivity and sustainability.
